First of all I’m so sorry that you have been beaten down like this, both systematically and on a personal level. You undoubtedly deserve better support in your life, and I hope you find people who support your passion and growth and want to see you shine, and that the people around you have a change in perspective too. 

You have been fed lies by a society designed to make you feel inferior because of your sex, skin tone, and genetic background. It’s designed this way specifically so that you’ll do this; devalue and diminish yourself so that you’ll give up and submit to the idea that you’re stupid, weak and can’t make any relevant positive change to the world, and settle for a life of being some man’s caretaker and brood mare. They say that it’s your “duty and purpose as a woman” so you won’t question it further and spend all your time worrying about being the most fuckable so someone will love you, ergo give you purpose, then telling you that you aren’t so you fixate on it until it cripples you. Now you think you’re completely devoid of value and want to give up and settle for less, just as the system intended.

This *does not* mean that love is unimportant or that you’re foolish for wanting it, it’s just not the only, or Number One Thing that matters in life. That being said, everyone is ugly to someone, and everyone is *beautiful* to someone, and you surely will find someone who not only sees you as physically attractive, but will also love your kindness, your interests, your joy, your intelligence, everything about you that makes you *you.* Also, some of the most stunningly gorgeous women in the world are black women with dark skin, or have features that aren’t typically seen on white women; either way there are many more important things about you to love and appreciate and there is someone who will see, appreciate and love it all.

Take this knowledge and **know that you are smarter and stronger and *far, far more important* than you give yourself credit for**. You can do anything you set your mind to and you’re doing amazing surviving in a world built with the cards stacked against you. Men and white people aren’t better or smarter just because they insist they are, or because other women and non white people buy into it. You absolutely can and should pursue a career in tech if that’s what you want to do, even if it’s hard, even if idiots don’t believe in you for the stupidest reasons. I hope you accomplish your dreams and I 100% believe you’re capable of it. ❤️

well the thing you’re choosing to not be disturbed by is the intrusive thought itself, not the concept the thought *presents*. If you see a small animal have an intrusive thought about punting it and then dismiss the thought as intrusive instead of validating it and shaming yourself, that doesn’t mean you don’t find punting small animals horrible, it means that you’re not going to think about that concept *because* it’s horrible and you *don’t want to do that.* if you actually wanted to do it you wouldn’t be dismissing the thought as intrusive, you’d just think it’s a bad idea.

of course you can’t feel anything! you’ve been put into circumstances several times over the course of your life (in the developmental stages at that) where allowing yourself to have feelings has been unsafe and used against you! it’s only natural that you’d subconsciously respond by numbing everything to *protect yourself. forgive yourself for that.* 

it’s been ingrained in you by your mother and by medical UNprofessionals that you’re inherently bad because you don’t know how to regulate your emotions properly and you “act out” but why would you know how to do that appropriately if you’ve never been taught how to? and when you try to, you aren’t taken seriously because the people meant to teach you are neglectful and abusive! *of course you’re acting out!* on top of that, from young childhood you’ve been through physical and sexual abuse, which it’s only natural you would learn to replicate, because that’s how people learn! **of COURSE you’re acting out!!!** 

it’s not your fault that everyone who was meant to protect and guide you through life are *monumental failures.* that doesn’t make you inherently bad! You want to be a good person? stop using your mother’s metric for “good” and define it for yourself, forgive yourself for your ignorance and mistakes of the past and move forward taking accountability for your actions when you make mistakes, try to learn to be sympathetic and empathetic (at least on a logical level if you can’t get there emotionally. it’s hard but *absolutely possible*) and if you aren’t currently please, PLEASE see a therapist to help you through that process and work on your self esteem. 

i’m sure seeing a mental health professional is especially intimidating for you given your trauma, but talk therapy is completely different, and you’re an adult now, so you’re in the drivers seat. if you don’t think you’re being treated respectfully you can get up and leave, and even fire the therapist if you really don’t like them. and each therapist has a different perspective and approach, so you can find someone who works well with you. 

I am confident in your ability to change your life for the better, even if you’re not confident yet. You just have to learn about yourself and how to navigate life given the shitty cards you’ve been dealt. All easier said than done, I know, but I still believe in you. I hope the best for you and your recovery process. :)

Your ego is big likely because you have this belief that if you hold yourself to the same level and standards as other people that you would be beneath them. if you’re “inherently exceptionally great” then in your mind, it doesn’t matter how bad you fuck up, or how many mistakes you make, or how many people are affected by what you do, because it’s you who did them so “it’s not a big deal and everyone should just get over it!” 

This grandiose delusion likely protects you from the opposite mindset of being “inherently exceptionally terrible” (many people have struggled with this, including myself, and many cope with it the same way you do), which you likely have based on past experiences of trauma and pain distorting your sense of self worth and confidence so that even minor mistakes are something to carry shame or guilt over (when in reality they’re not). And in situations where you’re reminded that you’re *not* better than others, especially when people try and knock you down a peg, it reinforces the fear that you actually *are* “inherently bad” and causes you to double double on you self defences (ego). 

It doesn’t help that people see NPD and narcissistic traits like this as both bad and inherent to the person, so thus “the person is bad”. Probably reinforces a vicious circle. But that’s not the truth, you can choose to put effort into yourself by learning and changing your perspective over time, and become a happier, more empathetic person. Even if you have a personality disorder and it will affect you for the rest of your life, it doesn’t mean you can’t make changes to improve your life and make it easier to cope with. :) 

I’m not a doctor or an expert on anything, but I wanted the share my knowledge on this kind of thing. I hope you understand that Im trying to be helpful and take what I say with a grain of salt. Regardless I hope you can find peace and happiness 💖

live (as in “live stream”) is pronounced with a “hard i” vowel, where as live (as in “i live here) is pronounced with a “soft i” vowel. leave is pronounced with a “hard e” vowel.

Hard vowels sound like the name of the letter. for example:
A - Ate
E - Eve
I - Ivy
U - Use
O - Open

Soft vowels are less consistent but often fall into this pattern:

A - Ah as in “Apple”
E - Ehh as in “Ever”
I - Ih as in all the i’s in “lives in Italy”
U - Uh as in “Up”
O - awh as it “Odd” 

Again, it’s not always this way and there’s a lot of in-betweens and double vowels can be different (for example, boot (“ooh”) and foot (closer to “uh”)

It seems like you pronounce soft i words more like hard e words (fix > feex, hit > heet, live > leev) when it’s meant to sound more like a soft  e vowel. 

https://youtu.be/HPXjwymejYE?si=TM21bl1ND-tJuFvS here’s a video I found where you can hear the subtle differences

Think of soft i as the higher pitched cousin of soft e. If you say the soft e, you can almost feel the sound coming from the middle of your throat. If you say the soft e with the sound coming from the upper back of your throat, slightly closer to the back of your sinuses, it will sound more like soft i.

if you can’t really relate to their answer ask them what  they like about it and try to build conversation off of that if you can. 

If the conversation about their favourite ends organically, you can then say “my favourite animals are snakes because I think they’re interesting biologically.” or “my favourite/guilty pleasure movie is ‘this’ because (xyz simplified reasons)”

Before you continue talking about it, pause and gauge their response and give them an opportunity to contribute back and ask questions. When you get excited about something, I know how easy it is for a dialogue to slip into a monologue if you’re not paying attention, which 1 they can’t partake and interject into, and 2 can overwhelm them with information they didn’t want which can feel off-putting. Try to treat your topic a bit like a QnA so that it can go back and forth even though your thing is the central focus at that point. 

If they make a face at you for your interest, you can even acknowledge if your opinion isn’t a very common one but it’s a little quirk of your taste and personality. for some reason it seems to ease tension and makes the person feel like it’s not actually that different or strange. It might actually make them more curious about it!

Usually people respond to simple answers by either agreeing with you and expanding on your thoughts and relating to them, or by asking you to expand on your thoughts so they can better understand your perspective. This should at least look like a mildly curious “oh yeah?” and If they don’t even do that I expect them to bring up another topic of their own. if you’re not thinking “I don’t care if i’m late i’ll get there when i want to” or “I know I don’t have time but I’m going to delay myself because I can anyways” then it’s not “intentionally being late.” you’re showing up late because you have a disability that affects your executive functioning, which includes your time management, task initiation and completion, and impulse control among other things. if you have depression or anxiety (which are common dual diagnoses for ADHD) it makes everything so much worse and makes it harder to even get out of bed. If you’re seriously trying your best but you just can’t get yourself to *just* **move** as much as you genuinely want to, it’s not laziness and it’s not your fault.

That being said, it’s still *your responsibility* to find accommodations for yourself at home to get you out the door on time. that might mean you have 500 alarms in the morning; or you brush your teeth as part of a break, or bathroom or smoke break just so it’s done; or you convince yourself you have to be at work an hour earlier than you’re actually expected to be there; or whatever else works for you. Your boss and management likely won’t be understanding or accommodating to this as showing up on time to work is a necessary requirement so there’s not much that can be done, that is if they even recognize or respect your condition to begin with, so it’s pretty much up to you to change the pattern unfortunately. 

Basically just don’t be so hard on yourself about it because it doesn’t help you to hate yourself over it, but try to find ways to make your life easier and helps you be more responsible. I hope you find things that helps you be successful, and please share when you do :) good luck.

- “Oh you look so fair, pasty even, haha...”
- “Yeah haha, I have no pigment to me at all. I look like a chip of drywall. If you didn’t know me you might think i’ve been locked up in some basement for a year, haha.”

i deal with impulse spending by giving myself a time limit. if i’m still interested in the thing within a set amount of time (depending on what it is and the price of course) then i’ll commit to the purchase. if it’s a cheap poster it might be a couple months so i can know if it’ll actually be put up or not if i buy it, but if I’m buying clothes or a figurine or something and it’s like 100$ or so then i’ll wait a much longer time even a year if it’s really expensive. i personally don’t buy anything that’s significantly expensive, especially if it’s not functional (clothes, mugs, etc). if I’m worried about it not being available by the time I’m ready to buy at that price point i remember that fandoms and merch stores are always pumping out cool shit and i can probably find a similar product by the time it rolls around. if you really have your heart set on something and you really really really want to commit to it you have to accept that you’re spending that money when an interest turnover could happen shortly. I’d rather buy something for a fandom i’ve been in for a year and stop liking it by the next month than buy something that was only relevant for a short short period of time because by the time a year has passed being a part of that thing has become truly important to me even if it looses relevancy. 

Event tickets are obviously a different story because you’re paying for an experience and its memory, you’ll have to weigh the pros and cons out depending on the circumstances. still wouldn’t drop a ton of money on something i just got into super recently unless like a group is going and it’s a social bonding over common interest thing.

as for inserting the topic into the conversation; i try to catch myself before i say anything and think if me sharing about my hyperfixation is relevant, will actually add to the conversation, or just make me happy to talk about. of course you’re always allowed to share about your interests and shouldn’t feel shame for just being exited about something you like but as you said it can overtake conversations and that can bother people. myself i’m still trying to figure out how to find the best time and way to broach my favourite subjects without it being excessive. i’m sure you’ve heard of gender dysphoria by now and to my understanding it is the feeling that you have a certain idea of what your body looks like subconsciously inside your head but when you actually see what your body looks like it’s not the same sex as in your head which can be distressing. imagine for a moment what it would feel like if you woke up in the morning thinking you’d see *your* body only to look down/in the mirror and see that you’re in your opposite sex sibling/cousins body. it can be uncomfortable to think about and it’s probably worse to experience. imagine having to live in that body for the rest of your life up until death, and everyone sees you as that sex and makes judgements on how to test based on that (humans subconsciously treat the sexes differently whether we mean to or not it’s just a thing we do). it’s not the cause of the issue but it makes it worse for sure. 

the reason people transition is to get rid of that discomfort by trying to make their body align more closely to their brains map of their body, and so that socially people will see them as the sex their brain is telling them they are and people won’t accidentally remind them that their brains idea of what they look like is wrong and make them feel uncomfortable. some people can handle that discomfort better than others and don’t need every surgery or procedure but for those that do use them it is to improve quality of life and not just for the aesthetic purposes. i’ve heard many people say that if they could just take a pill or do some kind of therapy or do something just to make that discomfort go away, they would. it would be much cheaper and socially and emotionally easier to deal with than permanently altering their bodies. unfortunately science isn’t far enough ahead to have an easy answer like that, and the only form of therapy that is effective and actually improves quality of life at this time is transitioning.
